# Accessibility Design Review: LiveSearch Component **VERDICT: REVISE** **Overall Assessment**: The `LiveSearch` component attempts a hybrid between an ARIA combobox and a navigation search dropdown, but suffers from conflicting ARIA roles, an invisible focus indicator, and broken composite widget focus semantics. Placing interactive `` elements inside `role="option"` breaks screen reader expectations, while CSS `outline: none` with an imperceptible `1.09:1` background color shift completely undermines keyboard operability. --- ### Pre-commitment Predictions Before reviewing this search dropdown implementation, the predicted accessibility issues were: 1. **Focus management mismatch**: Moving focus directly into result elements versus retaining focus in the input using `aria-activedescendant`. 2. **Missing or incomplete Combobox semantics**: `` missing `role="combobox"` while having `aria-expanded` and `aria-controls`. 3. **Invalid role nesting**: Placing navigation links (``) inside `role="listbox"` / `role="option"`. 4. **Focus indicator suppression**: Custom CSS zeroing out `:focus` outlines on result items. 5. **Tab order pollution**: Every result link remaining a Tab stop instead of acting as a single composite widget. *Outcome*: All five predicted issues are present in the component. --- ### Perspective Alarm Levels | Perspective | Alarm Level | Trigger Signal | |:---|:---:|:---| | **Screen reader** | **HIGH** | `role="option"` wrapping `` strips link semantics; `` lacks `role="combobox"`; missing `aria-selected`. | | **Keyboard-only** | **HIGH** | `outline: none` on results with `1.09:1` contrast; all results are in standard Tab sequence; no blur/click-outside dismiss. | | **Low vision** | **HIGH** | Focus indicator fails WCAG 2.4.13 with `1.09:1` contrast against white container background. | | **Cognitive** | **MEDIUM** | Escape clears entire query and results abruptly; no visual cue explaining ArrowDown navigates results. | | **Vestibular & motion** | **LOW** | No motion or animated transitions present. | | **Auditory access** | **LOW** | No audio or video content. | | **Environmental contrast** | **HIGH** | Focus background `#eff6ff` on `#ffffff` is functionally invisible in bright ambient light. | --- ## Critical Findings ### 1. Focus Indicator on Result Links Fails WCAG 2.4.7 and 2.4.13 * **Code Reference**: CSS lines 58–63 (`ul[role="listbox"] a:focus`) * **Impacted Users**: Keyboard-only, Low vision, Cognitive * **WCAG / APG Citation**: WCAG 2.4.7 Focus Visible (Level A), WCAG 2.4.13 Focus Appearance (Level AAA / 2.2 Best Practice) * **Confidence**: HIGH #### Evidence ```css ul[role="listbox"] a:hover, ul[role="listbox"] a:focus { background: #eff6ff; color: #1d4ed8; outline: none; } ``` #### Why This Matters When a user presses `ArrowDown` to navigate into results, `firstLink.focus()` is called. The CSS strips the focus indicator via `outline: none;` and applies `background: #eff6ff;` against the container's `#ffffff` background. The contrast ratio between `#eff6ff` (RGB 239, 246, 255) and `#ffffff` is **1.09:1**, far below the required 3:1 minimum contrast change. Sighted keyboard users cannot perceive which search result has focus. #### Fix Retain a prominent 2px solid outline with at least 3:1 contrast against `#ffffff`: ```css ul[role="listbox"] a:focus { background: #eff6ff; color: #1d4ed8; outline: 2px solid #2563eb; outline-offset: -2px; } ``` --- ### 2. Invalid ARIA Role Nesting: Interactive `` Inside `role="option"` * **Code Reference**: `LiveSearch.jsx:136-143` * **Impacted Users**: Screen reader users (NVDA, JAWS, VoiceOver) * **WCAG / APG Citation**: WCAG 4.1.2 Name, Role, Value (Level A), WAI-ARIA 1.2 Specification (`option` role) * **Confidence**: HIGH #### Evidence ```jsx
  • handleResultKeyDown(e, index)} > {result.title}
    • ``` #### Why This Matters Per the WAI-ARIA specification, elements with `role="option"` have presentational children (`Children Presentational: true`). Interactive elements such as `` are **forbidden** inside `role="option"`. Screen readers announce these items as selectable options in a listbox rather than links to external documents. Users will not hear that activating the item navigates to a new page, nor will screen reader shortcut keys for links (e.g., `U` in NVDA/JAWS) locate them. Furthermore, none of the options define `aria-selected`, which is mandatory for options inside a `listbox`. #### Fix Choose one of two coherent architectural patterns: 1. **Navigation Search List (Recommended for Search to URLs)**: Remove `role="listbox"` and `role="option"` entirely. Treat the dropdown as a standard list of links (`
      ` and `
    • `), retaining arrow-key navigation or standard Tab navigation. 2. **WAI-ARIA 1.2 Combobox with Selection**: Use `role="option"` on `
    • `, remove the nested ``, use `aria-selected`, and navigate programmatically via `window.location` on Enter or selection. --- ## Major Findings ### 3. Missing `role="combobox"` on `` * **Code Reference**: `LiveSearch.jsx:110-120` * **Impacted Users**: Screen reader users * **WCAG / APG Citation**: WCAG 4.1.2 Name, Role, Value (Level A), WAI-ARIA APG Combobox Pattern * **Confidence**: HIGH #### Evidence ```jsx 0} autoComplete="off" /> ``` #### Why This Matters An `` has the implicit role of `searchbox`. In WAI-ARIA 1.2, `aria-expanded` is not an allowed attribute on `role="searchbox"`. Without explicit `role="combobox"`, screen readers do not announce that the input controls an expandable suggestion popup, nor do they announce its expanded/collapsed state when typing. #### Fix Add `role="combobox"` and specify `aria-haspopup="listbox"` (or `aria-haspopup="dialog"`/`"true"`): ```jsx 0} aria-controls="search-results-list" aria-autocomplete="list" /> ``` --- ### 4. Tab Sequence Pollution in Composite Widget * **Code Reference**: `LiveSearch.jsx:136-143`, `handleKeyDown:43-58` * **Impacted Users**: Keyboard-only users * **WCAG / APG Citation**: WCAG 2.4.3 Focus Order (Level A), WAI-ARIA APG Design Patterns * **Confidence**: HIGH #### Why This Matters Because `` elements have `href` and no `tabindex="-1"`, every rendered result is an active Tab stop. If a query returns 10 results, pressing `Tab` from the search input forces the keyboard user to step through all 10 links sequentially before reaching the next section of the page. In a true composite widget or combobox, the popup represents a single tab stop, or pressing `Tab` dismisses the popup and tabs past it. #### Fix Set `tabIndex={-1}` on all result links, keeping them accessible strictly via Arrow keys while allowing `Tab` from the input or results to advance directly past the search component. --- ### 5. Missing Dismissal on Blur / Click-Outside * **Code Reference**: `LiveSearch.jsx:104-148` * **Impacted Users**: Low vision, Keyboard, Mouse users * **WCAG / APG Citation**: WCAG 3.2.1 On Focus, WCAG 1.3.2 Meaningful Sequence * **Confidence**: HIGH #### Why This Matters When the user clicks outside the component or tabs away to other content, the dropdown list remains open (`results.length > 0`) indefinitely. Because the dropdown is `position: absolute; z-index: 100`, it persistently obscures underlying page content. #### Fix Add a click-outside listener and/or an `onBlur` container handler (checking `relatedTarget`) to close the results and reset `aria-expanded` to `false` when focus departs the component. --- ## Minor Findings & Enhancements * **Identical Live Region Text Not Re-announced (WCAG 4.1.3 - MINOR)**: `LiveSearch.jsx:122-132`: If typing a new character updates the filtered result set but the count remains identical (e.g., 2 results -> 2 results), the live region's text content (`"2 results found"`) does not mutate. Most screen readers will remain silent, failing to confirm that the search re-executed. * *Fix*: Include the query term in the status string: `"{count} results found for '{query}'"`. * **Missing `aria-busy` during Debounced Search (Enhancement)**: `LiveSearch.jsx:32-39`: During the 300ms debounce and asynchronous search execution, there is no `aria-busy="true"` on the input or status container. Adding `aria-busy={isSearching}` clarifies that input processing is pending. * **Aggressive Escape Key Behavior (Cognitive Accessibility - Minor)**: `LiveSearch.jsx:52-57`: Pressing `Escape` simultaneously clears the query text, empties the results array, and resets the input. A two-stage dismissal is standard: the first `Escape` dismisses the dropdown results while keeping the typed query intact; a second `Escape` clears the query. --- ## What's Missing (Gap Analysis) 1. **Missing `aria-selected` State**: When using `role="option"`, AT expects `aria-selected="true|false"` to identify the active item. Currently, neither the DOM focus nor `aria-selected` is coordinated. 2. **Missing `Home` / `End` Keyboard Navigation**: In the results list, users cannot jump to the first or last result via standard APG list navigation keys (`Home`/`End`). 3. **Missing `form` Semantics**: The search input is not contained within a `
      ` or `` element. Screen reader users navigating by landmarks cannot locate the search feature. --- ## Multi-Perspective Notes * **Screen Reader User**: Confusing mental model. The input announces as a search field but has unannounced dropdown attributes. Results announce as options rather than links, hiding the fact that pressing `Enter` will trigger a page load to a new URL. * **Keyboard-Only User**: Trapped in high-friction navigation. The focus indicator on results is completely invisible due to `outline: none`. Tabbing from the input forces navigation through every single link. * **Low Vision User**: The `#eff6ff` highlight on `#ffffff` is imperceptible. Magnification users cannot tell which item is active when arrowing through results. * **Cognitive Accessibility**: Accidental Escape key presses delete all query text without confirmation or undo. --- ## Verdict Justification **REVISE**: The developer's intention to keep focus in the input during typing is sound and aligns with industry best practices (APG Combobox / Search autocomplete). However, the implementation conflates an ARIA `listbox` with a standard navigation list, removes the keyboard focus outline with no visible contrast alternative, leaves all results in the default Tab order, and lacks blur dismissal. Correcting the focus outline, removing the invalid `role="option"` from links, and adding `role="combobox"` will bring this component to production accessibility standards.
